without complying with civil service requirements.

died on June 6, 1924, after many years of faithful and efficient service in the

head:
Executive Ote?
Physical requirements for examination for rural carrier are hereby waived to
permit examination of Mr. William Anderson for the position of rural carrier at
Bemidji, Minnesota. Mr. Anderson's application for the examination which was
held on April 26, 1924, was not accepted because it showed that he had suffered the
loss of his right foot; that he was fitted with an artificial foot and that he could
stand on his feet all day.
The regulations prohibit acceptance of an application for rural carrier exani-e
nation from any one who has lost a foot, except in the case of honorably discharged
ex-service men who have been trained by the Veterans Bureau for the position of
rural carrier. The Postmaster General requested that the Civil Service Commission
waive the usual physical requirements in favor of Mr. Anderson, but the Commis-
sion is without power to do so.
The Civil Service Commission does not concur in recommending this order.
For charity.
CALVIN COOLIDGE
TuSi WHTE HOUSE,
August 29, 1924.

reinstated as operatives in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, without regard
to the length of time they have been separated from the service.

Paragraph 6, Subdivision XI, Schedule A, of positions excepted from exami-
nation under the civil service rules, is hereby amended to permit the appointment
of three additional assistants to the Secretary in the Office of the Secretary of
Commerce. The paragraph as amended will read as follows:
6. Four assistants to the Secretary in the Office of the
Secretary of Commerce..,
This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of Commerce
who states that the positions involve duties which are peculiarly personal and
confidential, and are similar to the position of Assistant to the Secretary of the
Interior which was placed under paragraph 25, Subdivision VIII, of Schedule A
by the Order of April 21, 1911, and are similar generally to the position of private
secretary or confidential clerk provided in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Subdivision I of
Schedule A. The Civil Service Commission is unable to concur in the recom-
